questions.prompt: The soldiers broke the enemy's line and poured across the river.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs aciem hostium rūpērunt et trāns flūmen sē fūdērunt.

questions.prompt: Once the fierce tribes had been conquered, the general fortified the walls.
questions.answer: Ferōcibus gentibus victīs, dux mūrōs mūnīvit.

questions.prompt: When the trumpet sounded, dread touched the hearts of all.
questions.answer: Cum tuba cecinit, timor omnium corda tetigit.

questions.prompt: Our men drove the enemy from the camp with great slaughter.
questions.answer: Nostrī hostēs ex castrīs magnā caede pepulērunt.

questions.prompt: The pupil learned the song which the teacher had taught.
questions.answer: Discipulus carmen didicit quod magister docuerat.

questions.prompt: The dog bit the thief who stood before the door.
questions.answer: Canis fūrem momordit quī ante iānuam stetit.

questions.prompt: The general bent the battle line toward the left wing.
questions.answer: Dux aciem in cornū sinistrum flexit.

questions.prompt: The priests spread garlands upon the sacred altars.
questions.answer: Sacerdōtēs serta in ārīs sacrīs strāvērunt.

questions.prompt: We scorned the threats of the cruel tyrant.
questions.answer: Minās crūdēlis tyrannī sprēvimus.

questions.prompt: The soldiers allowed the captives to return home unharmed.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs captīvōs incolumēs domum redīre sīvērunt.

questions.prompt: The enemy destroyed the city which our ancestors had loved.
questions.answer: Hostēs urbem dēlēvērunt quam maiōrēs nostrī amāverant.

questions.prompt: The old man, once the cups had been filled, praised the gods.
questions.answer: Senex, pōculīs complētīs, deōs laudāvit.

questions.prompt: The girl bound the wounds of the wounded soldier with care.
questions.answer: Puella vulnera mīlitis vulnerātī cūrā vīnxit.

questions.prompt: The river burst its banks and flooded the fields.
questions.answer: Flūmen rīpās rūpit et agrōs inundāvit.

questions.prompt: When night fell, the weary travelers fell asleep.
questions.answer: Cum nox vēnit, fessī viātōrēs obdormīvērunt.

questions.prompt: The victor spared the citizens who had thrown away their weapons.
questions.answer: Victor cīvibus pepercit quī arma abiēcerant.

questions.prompt: The recruits learned to endure hardship in the winter camp.
questions.answer: Tīrōnēs labōrem in hībernīs castrīs patī didicērunt.

questions.prompt: Having conquered the enemy, the general bound the captives with heavy chains.
questions.answer: Hostibus victīs, dux captīvōs gravibus catēnīs vīnxit.

questions.prompt: The crops grew slowly because the fields lacked rain.
questions.answer: Segetēs lentē crēvērunt quia agrī imbre carēbant.

questions.prompt: The frightened soldiers fled while the trumpets sounded through the night.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs perterritī fūgērunt dum tubae per noctem strepēbant.

questions.prompt: The gods created the world and nourished the human race.
questions.answer: Deī mundum genuērunt et genus hūmānum aluērunt.

questions.prompt: At first light the traveler turned his steps toward the pine grove.
questions.answer: Viātor prīmā lūce gressūs ad pīneum nemus flexit.

questions.prompt: Fear increased the danger, and terror grew in the trembling city.
questions.answer: Timor perīculum auxit, et terror in trepidā urbe crēvit.

questions.prompt: Victory helped our allies, whom fortune had long deserted.
questions.answer: Victōria sociōs nostrōs iūvit, quōs fortūna diū dēseruerat.

questions.prompt: The storm burst the clouds, and rain fell upon the weary fields.
questions.answer: Tempestās nūbēs rūpit, et imber in fessōs agrōs cecidit.
